concept: Separate-stack cost floors: Pinecone, OpenSearch Serverless NextGen, Elastic Serverless, S3 Vectors
summary: Source-anchored research for Separate-stack cost floors: Pinecone, OpenSearch Serverless NextGen, Elastic Serverless, S3 Vectors. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: NextGen scale-to-zero requires a collection group. AWS documents 10–30 seconds of latency on the first request to each reactivated component; a nonzero configured minimum avoids scale-to-zero. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Scale-to-zero is available only to NextGen collections in a collection group. The documented idle timer considers requests across the group; search and indexing sleep and wake independently. The first request to each sleeping component can incur 10–30 seconds of provisioning latency. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

OpenSearch Serverless NextGen has no mandatory OCU floor when collection-group minimums are zero. Indexing and search independently scale to zero after ten idle minutes; compute and storage are separate charges, so zero OCU does not mean free retained data. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Elastic’s pricing page illustrates a 2 GB development workload at $24/month On-demand or $27/month Performant, and a 20 GB production workload at $190 or $210 respectively. These are workload examples with stated utilization assumptions, not guaranteed minimums or caps. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The current S3 Vectors US East (N. Virginia) example uses $0.06/GB-month storage, $0.20/GB uploaded, $2.50 per million query API calls, processed-data tiers of $0.004/$0.002/$0.0004 per TB at 100K and 10M vector boundaries, and $0.01/GB returned. PUTs have a minimum billable size of 128 KB; batching small writes can reduce their effective cost. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

S3 Vectors charges query processing from indexed vector data, keys and filterable metadata; non-filterable metadata is excluded. PUTs have a 128 KB minimum billable size. Batching and index partitioning affect cost independently of an application's vector quantization. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Meltwater reports that moving 1.23 TB of sentence embeddings to S3 Vectors in July 2026 reduced that workload's run cost by roughly 90%. The engineering account identifies append-only, time-partitioned, query-light data as the fit. This is a workload-specific production report, not a measured saving against Atlas automatic quantization. (low confidence)

Inference from the pricing models: compare a separate retrieval stack using plan fees, idle search capacity, stored data, query/ingest charges and synchronization services. OpenSearch Ingestion is billed separately and can be paused; quantization savings alone cannot establish which full application architecture costs less. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Elastic Serverless charges for allocated resources rather than a simple per-query tariff. Search demand, dataset size, and Search Power influence search allocation, so a query count alone is insufficient to infer the bill or a universal monthly floor. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

S3 Vectors query processing charges depend on the queried index’s vector count and average vector/key/filterable-metadata size, rather than only the top-k result count. Non-filterable metadata is excluded from processed bytes but can contribute to returned bytes. Therefore index partitioning and metadata design affect costs even at the same query count. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Pinecone Standard has a $50 monthly minimum applied toward usage; only usage beyond $50 increases that usage bill. Enterprise has a $500 monthly minimum. Treating $50 as an additional fixed fee on top of all metered usage misstates the published pricing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Pinecone offers free Starter and a $20/month flat-rate Builder plan. Treating $50/month as the minimum for every Pinecone application excludes these lower-entry plans; their usage and feature limits must be checked against the application. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The current AWS pricing page still specifies a Classic first-collection minimum of two OCUs with redundancy, or one OCU total for dev-test without redundant standby nodes, with further variation by data size and collection type. These Classic floors must not be transferred to NextGen. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Elastic's pricing page says idle Search VCUs retain a billed baseline determined by search-ready data and Search Power; On-demand lowers that baseline and idle ingest can scale to zero. Its engineering explainer adds that small, completely inactive search workloads can reach zero after fifteen minutes, while larger datasets need a warm minimum. An unconditional always-on Elastic compute floor is therefore not established. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

S3 pricing states no minimum charge. For S3 Vectors, storage and upload charges depend on logical vector bytes, keys, and metadata, and queries incur request, index-data-processed, and returned-data charges. A no-provisioned-compute-floor model still has continuing storage costs and workload-dependent request costs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

AWS's context-ontology-accelerator deployment guide warns that a zero NextGen minimum can increase HTTP 429 bulk-write throttling. Its implementation recommends a nonzero floor, for example two OCUs, for ingest-heavy environments and fails loudly on unrecoverable partial indexing. This is application-specific operational evidence, not a universal AWS minimum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

OpenSearch Ingestion pipelines have their own compute meter, separate from Serverless indexing/search OCUs. AWS allows configuring pipeline minimum and maximum OCUs and explicitly pausing a pipeline to stop its OCU consumption; collection scale-to-zero alone does not remove pipeline charges. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Elastic’s current pricing FAQ says idle projects retain a search baseline tied to searchable dataset size and Search Power; On-demand lowers that baseline with more variable latency. The FAQ says ingest VCUs scale to zero without ingestion, while the engineering blog qualifies this with an exception for thousands of indices. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For Atlas quantization comparisons, distinguish a plan minimum, an allocated-compute baseline, and usage-metered storage/request costs. Compression of vector memory alone does not establish that a separate stack’s bill will fall below a plan floor or that two systems deliver equivalent recall, latency, and freshness. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
